correctness.rationale: For every fixed integer multiplicity m, Weyl unitarity gives the exact block Gram/leakage identity. The leakage Taylor entries have a unique minimal-order exterior minor at each p; its nonzero falling-factorial Vandermonde determinant proves that the product of the p largest singular values has sharp order \(r^{p^2}\) with an explicit coefficient. Dividing successive products gives all m singular-value exponents and constants; the conversion to paired Gram eigenvalues is algebraically exact. Strict positivity at r>0 follows from exponential-polynomial independence; compressed displacement invertibility follows from triangular factorization. Separately calculated high-precision transition amplitudes and full Gram matrices passed 717 assertions; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two-site Hermite interpolation in Gaussian Fock space is a natural finite information-recovery task. The precise rate of the smallest Riesz bound dictates worst-case coefficient noise gain; the theorem quantifies it by the sharp \(r^{4m-2}\) law and nontrivial factorial constant for every multiplicity. More strongly, all m modes exhibit distinct optimal exponents \(r^{4p-2}\), not a single generic nonsingularity statement or a special-case calculation. This provides structurally motivated quantitative interpolation information absent from the inspected density/geometric theorems.
